The starting point

What is EDC?

Electronic Data Capture — the act of transcribing data into a system
based on what is already recorded in the source documents.

Hence the entire concept of Source Data Verification exists — because EDC captures a copy, not the source.

The implication:

EDC was never designed to be the data platform.
It was designed to be the data entry point.

Context

How We Got Here

Early Days
  • Purpose-built as an EDC platform
  • Monolithic design — fast to build, simple to deploy
  • Core: Clinic, Admin, Designer
  • Single SQL database (MySQL + XPO)
Growth Phase
  • ePRO, lab integrations, reporting layered on
  • Each new consumer built its own data sync
  • WCF-based integrations tied to legacy protocols
  • New capabilities added inside the monolith
Where We Are Now
  • Only ~25% of trial data flows through the platform
  • 75% of data sources remain disconnected
  • N apps = N separate sync pipelines
  • Export is the only place data gets unified
Structural issues

EDC as a data model — inherent limitations

Data entry as the bottleneck
Data exists only after someone types it in. The system waits for the human.
Discrete data points, no streaming
Visit-based, form-based. No concept of continuous data from devices, labs, or wearables.
Relational data → monolithic coupling
The write model dictates the read model. How you enter data determines how you can use it.
Async access to analysis-ready data
You can enter data now, but you can't use it now. Batch exports are the only way out.
What this means at Viedoc

The pain we feel today

  • Long-running exports — batch process that blocks downstream work and scales poorly
  • Reports syncs data daily — makes exports work even harder; built on R Shiny we're decommissioning
  • Viedoc Coder — syncs data changes continuously, and first-pass changes go through the export path
  • Every new app builds its own sync — each one slightly different, all hard to maintain
  • FormSave/edit code is deeply coupled — it works, but the write path shouldn't dictate how consumers read data
  • The pyramid problem — EDC sits at the apex as data gatekeeper; 75% of trial data is outside the EDC

Foundation

Principles

  • Timely without post-processing — consumers get data ready to use, not raw extracts to transform
  • Event-based — every change is an event, stored immutably, replayable
  • Multiple views, same truth — export, API, AI, dashboards — all from one event stream
  • Decoupled — write side (EDC forms) and read side (data consumers) evolve independently
  • External event contracts — outside consumers subscribe to curated published events, not raw domain internals
  • Auditable by design — the event log is the audit trail (21 CFR Part 11)

Migration strategy

Strangler Fig, not Big Bang

We don't rewrite — we grow around. Each phase delivers independent value.

1
Shadow
Event-source the EDC's data into a parallel store. CDC sync creates domain events. Build first materialized views.
2
Migrate consumers
Internal apps read from the vault instead of the EDC. Export, Reports, Coder switch over. EDC still the write path.
3
Data platform
Vault becomes primary. EDC is one source among many. External sources feed in directly.
What we're NOT proposing
Not a rewrite. Not replacing the EDC. Not a big-bang migration. The EDC continues to do what it does well — capture data.
Why not just improve the export?
The export is a symptom, not the disease. A faster export still doesn't solve N×N syncs, real-time access, or external data sources.
Core pattern

Event Sourcing — how data flows

Source
MySQL

→

Projections
→

Views
Events are the source of truth
Immutable, append-only. Every state change captured as a domain event.
CDC from MySQL audit tables
Watermark-based sync per domain area. Idempotent — natural keys prevent duplicates.
Views can be rebuilt anytime
Replay events to regenerate any view. Schema evolution via upcasters — no migration.

We don't copy the database — we translate relational records into domain events.

Read side

Materialized Views — data ready to consume

Projections continuously maintain optimized views — examples from the POC:

Clinical Data
Every data point with decoded values, design context, audit metadata
Subject Status
Enrollment state, screening dates, site assignment
Event Dates
Visit schedule, planned vs actual dates
Queries
Open/closed/resolved query status per data point
SDV Coverage
Source data verification status by site, subject, form
Review Status
Clinical and data review tracking

Each projection reads events and maintains its own optimized shape. Error-tolerant: one bad event is logged, projection continues.

The views ARE the "export" — always current, always queryable.

Proof of concept

Export — cell-for-cell validation

691,431 / 691,431
cells matched — pilot study, V492 format
What was validated
35 sheets · All column types · Split columns (__2 suffix) · Checkbox expansion · Coded values · Design version resolution · System columns · Audit metadata
Why this matters
If the vault's export matches the EDC's export field-by-field, the underlying data is trustworthy. Every other consumer reads from the same views.
Known edge cases
33/35 sheets are cell-perfect. 2 sheets have extra rows from a known EDC filter edge case — documented, not a data issue.
